  "text": "He took the last piece from his plate. The butter had softened enough to leave a shine on his finger.

She watched him eat, then pulled the bag towards her.

“This one?”

It was smaller than the first, blue inside where the corner had torn. There was no stamp.

“Careful,” he said.

“I can open an envelope.”

But she handed it to him.

Inside was a key wrapped in a sheet of paper. He unfolded the paper over his plate. A few crumbs caught in the crease.

“What does it say?”

“Only an address.”

“Read it.”

He did. She looked towards the window, where the neighbour's washing had begun to turn in the wind.

“That's gone,” she said.

“The street?”

“The house. There was a chemist on the corner. They took the whole row.”

He set the key beside the receipt. Its stem was longer than he expected, its teeth blunt and uneven.

“Did we live there?”

“Not you.”

A van stopped outside. For a moment its engine made the spoons tremble against one another in the drawer.

She picked up the photograph of the car.

“I know that hat,” she said.

He waited while she brought it close, then held it farther away.

“Your father had one like it.”

“Is it him?”

“No. His brim went down at the front.”

The van moved off. She put the photograph on top of the address.

“There's jam if you want it.”

He turned the key over. On the other side, near the bow, a small number had been struck into the metal.

She reached across and covered it with her hand."
